c380ec0b05098f46: Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself.

This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28, for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. If none of those are quite what you’re looking for, we’ve also found good deals on models from Roborock, Dreame, and more, with picks below for a variety of budgets and cleaning needs.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
$1499.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (with Dreame W10 vacuum)

The Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent robot vacuum for hardwood floors. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and a good vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most models. Read our review.

Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.

The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.

With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.

The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

The Freo X Ultra features spinning triangular mop pads and can swing slightly to reach baseboards. Its large charging dock holds two big water tanks, while Narwal’s disposable onboard bin compresses the dust. It’s also relatively quiet when it returns to the dock, and its anti-tangle brush and 8,200Pa of suction perform well on most carpets.

2a4644e2a98b697b: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) could get off to a winning start in the state election, with almost half of the 82 seats up for grabs likely to go uncontested based on the prospective candidates announced ahead of today's nomination day.
Based on announcements by political coalitions, parties and individuals, 40 seats could see only one candidate, with all the candidates in those constituencies representing GPS.
Sarawak's record for the highest number of uncontested victories was set in 1996, when Barisan Nasional won 19 of the then 62 seats unopposed.

The 40 constituencies identified ahead of today's nomination process would therefore be more than double the previous record if all the prospective candidates were confirmed as the sole nominees in their respective seats.
However, the actual number of uncontested seats will only be known after the nomination process is completed and the returning officers have confirmed the candidates.
Based on announcements made so far, GPS has named candidates for all 82 seats, while Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS) will contest 26 seats and Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) 12.

DAP yesterday announced that it would contest two additional seats, with Dewan Rakyat Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng contesting Bawang Assan and Sarawak DAP secretary Alan Ling Siee Kiong standing in Senadin.
The decision came after PKR announced that it would not contest in the Sarawak election, bringing DAP's total number of seats in the polls to 14.

As of Thursday, two people had also announced their intention to contest as independent candidates. They included Anyi Jana, who announced that he had quit Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and would defend his Ngemah seat as an independent.
GPS had earlier announced that it would field a new candidate, Alexander Donald, in the constituency.

The prospect of a large number of uncontested seats has, however, raised concerns among electoral reform group Rise of Social Efforts, particularly following decisions by BN, PKR, Pas and Amanah to sit out the election.

It said uncontested victories would deny voters the opportunity to compare candidates and their policy offerings, evaluate the performance of incumbent representatives and use their votes to hold elected representatives accountable.
The prospect of GPS securing a sizeable number of seats without a contest has also raised questions over whether the coalition could form the next state government before polling day on Dec 12.
A simple majority in the 82-seat Sarawak Legislative Assembly requires at least 42 seats.

Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the commission had sought advice from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) on the next course of action should GPS secure enough uncontested victories during today's process to obtain a simple majority.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, however, said: "Let the process of the election be completed. We can't be certain at this juncture."
"We have to wait until tomorrow (today). The power to declare lies with the EC. We will see how it goes," he told the New Straits Times.

Meanwhile, former EC chairman Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Mohd Yusof said Regulation 25F of the Elections (Conduct of Elections) Regulations 1981 provided for the EC to declare a political party as having won the general election only after the official addition of votes and the declaration of results for all contested constituencies had been completed.
He said an election could only be considered completed after the vote-counting process had concluded and the results had been formally announced by the EC.
"In this situation, the election must proceed even if GPS has already secured a simple majority."
The state election will involve 2,058,781 registered voters, comprising 2,034,373 ordinary voters, 13,575 military personnel and their spouses, and 10,833 police and their spouses.

14139dc8051169a9: TAIPEI: Taiwanese people will flock to schools, temples and community centres on Saturday to cast their ballots in local elections, after the government warned of Chinese attempts to influence voters.
The elections, held every four years, will decide races for about 11,000 positions, including mayors and magistrates, across the island democracy's 22 cities and counties.
Polling stations open at 8am (0000 GMT) and close at 4pm, with results expected to be released in the evening.

Candidates have campaigned relentlessly for weeks, posing for selfies in night markets, waving from the back of pick-up trucks and appearing on talk shows in a bid to win over voters on issues ranging from transport and childcare to urban renewal.
The Kuomintang (KMT), Taiwan's oldest party and the one that favours closer ties with China, faces the challenge of defending the 14 city and county seats it won in 2022.
President Lai Ching-te's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) will be seeking to improve on the five seats it holds.
In Taipei, KMT Mayor Chiang Wan-an, who won by double digits last time and is seen as a potential future presidential candidate, is facing off against DPP rival Puma Shen.
Shen, an outspoken critic of China who is wanted by police there for alleged criminal "separatist activities", entered the race as the underdog.
But Shen managed to ride a political wave that has drawn huge turnouts at his rallies and frenzied demand for his campaign ribbons, badges and other goodies.
A Shen victory in the KMT's heartland could be seen as "quite shameful" in Beijing, said Austin Wang, a political science professor at the University of Nevada.
China claims Taiwan as part of its territory and has threatened to use force to seize the island.
Thousands of boisterous Chiang supporters holding flags and balloons attended a final rally on a major street on Friday night.
Shen hosted a mass online gathering that was watched by several hundred thousand people after a venue mix-up forced the cancellation of an outdoor event.
'VERY TIGHT'
Saturday's turnout of undecided and young voters will determine the outcome of the "very tight race", said Liu Jia-wei, a political science professor at National Taipei University.
A major upset could also be brewing in the mayoral election in New Taipei, Taiwan's largest city and another KMT stronghold.
In the run-up to election day, candidates from both major parties have steered clear of the threat posed by China, instead focusing on bread-and-butter issues.

But the Mainland Affairs Council, Taiwan's top policy body on China, has warned that Beijing has used a range of tactics to try to influence the outcome, including "cognitive warfare" and "transnational repression".
Beijing "will continue to closely monitor Taiwan's local political situation", Liu said.

While Taiwan's presidential elections are only 14 months away, analysts have cautioned that the local elections are not a reliable predictor of how people might vote in 2028, with history showing repeatedly that the reverse can happen.
But Saturday's results could influence the selection process for the KMT presidential candidate.
While the DPP is likely to rally behind Lai in his re-election bid, the KMT could begin debating its presidential ticket soon after the local elections, Liu said.
Among the most likely KMT candidates are outgoing Taichung Mayor Lu Shiow-yen and parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu.
KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, whose pro-Beijing stance and political style have alienated her from many in her party, is also seen as a potential challenger for the nomination.
But she could face pressure to step down from her position if the KMT performs poorly in the local elections.

eea89f38aadbbd80: KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged supply of non-halal chicken to Muslim consumers and two lawsuits seeking RM600 million in damages from technology giant Google were among this week's major court developments.

A poultry supply company, its two directors, a manager and an employee were charged over allegedly supplying more than 6.5 tonnes of processed chicken to Muslim consumers as halal when it was not. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) also sued Google over its alleged failure to address harmful content on YouTube.

A Libyan university student was charged with reckless driving that caused a retired soldier's death, while a gag order was issued in the criminal case involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
The High Court also dismissed a bid by two men to challenge the government's decision to remove blanket diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia.
Here are the week's major court cases and developments.
COMPANY DIRECTORS, STAFF CHARGED OVER NON-HALAL CHICKEN
A poultry supply company, its two directors, a manager and an employee were charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court on Tuesday over allegedly supplying non-halal chicken as halal to Muslim consumers.
The directors, Zafirah Abdul Karim, 36, and Bangladeshi Tanjena Akter Mollah, 36, and manager Hossain Saddam, 44, pleaded not guilty before judge Ainul Bashiirah Dona Don Biyajid.
Employee Abdul Rahim Ariff Ali, 34, also pleaded not guilty.
The charges involved 6,555kg of processed chicken. The company, its directors and manager were accused of supplying the chicken while the employee was accused of abetting the offence.
The offences were allegedly committed at a chicken processing facility in Puchong on Oct 30.
NST report: [Non-halal chicken: Company directors, staff charged over alleged supply to Muslim consumers]
MCMC SEEKS RM600MIL IN TWO LAWSUITS AGAINST GOOGLE
The MCMC filed two lawsuits against Google, seeking RM600 million in damages over its alleged failure to address harmful content on YouTube.
The first suit concerns content linked to online gambling, scams and fraud.
The second involves allegedly false and defamatory content published by blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo.
On Wednesday, the commission confirmed that it was seeking RM300 million in damages in each suit.
NST report: MCMC sues Google for RM600mil over harmful YouTube content
LIBYAN STUDENT CHARGED OVER RETIRED SOLDIER'S DEATH
Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him in English before magistrate Amalina Johar.
He was accused of driving a Proton Saga recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Jelatek here at 1am on Nov 21, causing the death of Mohd Hairezam Omar, 43.
The charge, under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, carries a jail term of between five and 10 years and a fine of between RM20,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
Ali was released on bail of RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties.
The court fixed Jan 28 next year for mention.
NST report: [Libyan student posts RM17,000 bail in fatal Jalan Jelatek crash]
COURT ISSUES GAG ORDER IN MCBA DIRECTOR-GENERAL'S CASE

The Sepang Magistrate's Court issued a gag order in the criminal case involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, who faces two charges of causing hurt to police personnel.
The order does not prevent the media from reporting on proceedings in open court.
It was granted on Wednesday following a defence application to prevent parties involved in the case from making public statements until the proceedings conclude.
On Oct 21, Shuhaily, 54, pleaded not guilty to two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to policemen Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Dirman, 25.
The offences were allegedly committed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28.
Both charges were framed under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Shuhaily is out on bail of RM3,000 for both charges.
NST report: [Shuhaily returns to court over assault charges]
TWO MEN FAIL IN BID TO CHALLENGE DIESEL SUBSIDY REMOVAL
The High Court on Wednesday dismissed an application by two men seeking leave to challenge the government's decision to remove blanket diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in June 2024.
Judge Datuk Norliza Othman ruled that the decision was a policy matter and was not justiciable.
Azhani Marlan @ Abd Halim and Mohd Hatta Sanuri filed the application on Oct 7, 2024, naming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and five others as respondents.
The Attorney-General's Chambers opposed the application, arguing that the granting or withdrawal of subsidies was not a right provided for under any written law.
The dismissal means the two men cannot proceed with their substantive judicial review application.
NST report: [High Court dismisses bid to challenge diesel subsidy removal]

2361945ccc160f2a: QATAR: New world champion Kimi Antonelli completed a Friday 'double top' ahead of team-mate George Russell as Mercedes dominated both practice sessions before Sunday's Qatar Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian, the sport's youngest champion and Italy's first since 1953, clocked a best lap of one minute and 23.077 seconds to outpace Russell by 0.127sec in a session interrupted by two red flags.

The Mercedes duo wound up four-tenths clear of the McLarens of outgoing world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, and the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton.
"I think it's going to be very close between me and George and then, of course, you can never write off Max and the others," said Antonelli.
"There have been already some weekends where we were very strong at the beginning and then, in qualifying, the others seemed to make a big step and get close.
"So, we just need to work and to keep working and keep improving and then we will try to be ready for tomorrow."
The stoppages came to clean up gravel after a Leclerc spin and to rescue Pierre Gasly's Alpine from a gravel trap, but there were few other dramas.

Russell worked hard to erase memories of his feud with Verstappen, and their clash in Las Vegas, an experience that left him praising the "values, grace and dignity" of former Mercedes team-mate Hamilton.
"He (Verstappen) is a ruthless competitor and I massively respect that," he told Sky Sports of Verstappen.
"But there's also Lewis Hamilton, who I've spent three years as team-mates with and watched my whole life.
"He is equally a ruthless competitor and an absolute animal behind the wheel, but he obviously has incredible values and grace and dignity."

Verstappen, who is seeking a fourth consecutive victory in Qatar after winning last Sunday's Las Vegas Grand Prix, was unhappy with his car as Red Bull seek to outscore Ferrari heavily to keep up their bid for second in the constructors's championship.
"The steering was quite heavy," said the Dutchman who is 37 points ahead of Hamilton in the chase to be runner-up to Antonelli.
"We're just not where we want to be and it feels a bit disconnected.... The gap to Mercedes is very big and they are very quick on the straights."
The Ferraris had a largely unhappy day with Leclerc spinning and depositing gravel across the track at Turn Eight, resulting in a red flag as the marshals cleaned up.

Gasly prompted the second red flag when he beached his Alpine in the gravel at Turn 14 while Hamilton's practice ended shortly after the restart when his Ferrari lost power, leading to the deployment of a virtual safety car.
fe4ed6e27e76e96a: MOSCOW: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country's fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin.
At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy.
"Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance," he said.
Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia's nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack.
Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm.
The submarines can operate in "any part of the world's oceans" while carrying a range of cruise missiles, he added.

abb02085f5e929eb: KUALA LUMPUR: The crippling of an interstate housebreaking gang linked to 15 cases, separate cable theft incidents in Kuala Lumpur and Melaka, and a road rage assault on a 62-year-old man in Terengganu were among the major crime stories reported this week.

Also in focus were the arrest of an enforcement officer suspected of facilitating the illegal entry of a foreigner at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and a Selangor operation that led to the arrest of three people and the seizure of six stolen vehicles.
Below are some of the cases reported this week.
INTERSTATE HOUSEBREAKING GANG LINKED TO 15 CASES CRIPPLED
Police have crippled an interstate housebreaking gang linked to 15 cases involving estimated losses of RM293,500 across four states, following the arrest of two suspects in Kuala Lumpur.

Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the two local men, aged 40 and 44, were arrested by the department's Intelligence and Operations Division (D4) in Taman City on Nov 16.
The arrests were made less than an hour after a break-in was reported at a house in Taman Rainbow, Jalan Ipoh, at noon on the same day.
Kumar said the gang was believed to have targeted unguarded terrace houses during the day, when their occupants were away.
Its members allegedly used vehicles fitted with false registration plates.

Police seized a black Toyota Camry fitted with false registration plates, mobile phones, tablets, watches, laptops, a closed-circuit television system, three sets of vehicle registration plates, RM1,000, four Touch 'n Go cards and a gold purchase receipt.
Bags, shoes, clothing, gloves and face masks believed to have been used in the break-ins were also seized.
Investigations linked the gang to seven break-ins in Selangor, five in Perak, two in Pahang and one in Kuala Lumpur.
Police have identified another suspected gang member, who remains at large.
NST report: [Interstate housebreaking gang linked to RM293,500 losses busted]
CABLE THIEVES SOUGHT AFTER THEFTS IN KL, MELAKA
Police are tracking down separate groups of cable thieves following incidents in Kuala Lumpur and Melaka, both of which were captured on video and circulated on social media.
In Kuala Lumpur, a group was seen cutting cables along Jalan Tun Razak, near TREC, in broad daylight. The suspects arrived in two vehicles.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said police received a report on the incident on Nov 21 after a 38-second video of the theft went viral on Threads.
He said the suspects fled after being approached by members of the public.
In a separate incident in Melaka, police pursued suspected cable thieves from Taman Malim Jaya to Rumbia after they were spotted opening a manhole cover on Nov 21.
Melaka Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the suspects fled in a dark blue Proton S70 and a white Toyota Hilux when they noticed police approaching.
The pursuit involved several police vehicles and passed through Taman Malim Jaya, Batu Berendam, Krubong and Cheng before reaching Rumbia in Alor Gajah.
Both vehicles managed to escape, and police are still tracking down the suspects.
NST report: [Cable thieves flee in Proton S70, Hilux after police chase]
NST report: [Police track down cable thieves near TREC]
THREE ARRESTED OVER ROAD RAGE ASSAULT ON ELDERLY MAN
Police have arrested three men suspected of assaulting a 62-year-old man following a road rage incident in Lorong Ikhwan, Jalan Pasir Panjang, Kuala Terengganu, on Nov 23.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred after a Perodua Alza allegedly rear-ended a Skoda driven by a woman.
He said the woman's husband got out of the vehicle to inspect the damage but was allegedly punched, elbowed and kicked by the three men.
The victim sustained injuries to his nose, mouth and face and was taken to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital for treatment.
Khairi said swift action by the Kuala Terengganu Criminal Investigation Department led to the arrest of the three suspects, aged between 39 and 44.

The suspects were remanded for four days to facilitate investigations under Section 325 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt. The offence carries a prison term of up to seven years and a fine upon conviction.

A 20-second video of the incident, which went viral on social media, showed a man wearing a black jacket and cap grabbing the victim's shoulder before elbowing him in the face by the roadside in the rain.
NST report: [Three arrested over road rage assault of elderly man in Terengganu]
THREE ARRESTED, SIX STOLEN VEHICLES SEIZED IN SELANGOR
Police have arrested three people, including a woman, and seized six vehicles believed to be linked to a vehicle theft syndicate operating in Kajang, Serdang and Kuala Langat.
Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the suspects, two men and a woman aged between 20 and 30, were arrested in a special operation on Nov 23.
The operation followed a report lodged over the theft of a Proton Iswara in Kajang Utama on Nov 22.
Police seized six vehicles between Nov 23 and 24: a Proton Iswara, Nissan Vanette, Proton Wira Aeroback, Mazda E2200 and two Toyota lorries.
Naazron said preliminary investigations found that all six vehicles were linked to theft cases in Kajang and Serdang.
The suspects were also believed to have been involved in other criminal cases in Kajang, Serdang and Kuala Langat.
All three had previous criminal records and drug-related offences and tested positive for methamphetamine in preliminary urine screening.
They have been remanded for four days to assist investigations, while police are tracking down several other suspects.
NST report: [Three arrested, six stolen vehicles seized in Kajang]
MCBA OFFICER ARRESTED FOR FACILITATING FOREIGN WOMAN'S ILLEGAL ENTRY
A Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer has been arrested for allegedly facilitating the illegal entry of a foreign woman without valid travel documents at KLIA Terminal 2.
MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain confirmed that the arrested civil servant was one of the agency's officers.
He said the arrest was made possible by a female MCBA officer who detected suspicious conduct involving her superior and took action.
Shuhaily praised the officer for reporting the alleged misconduct, describing her actions as an example of the integrity needed to address wrongdoing within the agency.
He said he intended to meet her personally and pledged his support, adding that he hoped more personnel would demonstrate similar courage.
The case came to light after an MCBA officer lodged a police report on Nov 17 over the illegal entry of a foreign woman through the arrival hall Immigration counter at KLIA Terminal 2.
Shuhaily said the arrested officer was in police custody and was believed to have been detained under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act.
NST report: [Shuhaily: Officer arrested over KLIA 2 security breach is MCBA personnel]

63d59ebdb3022f04: CAIRO: The son of Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya survived an assassination attempt by the Israeli military on Friday, senior Hamas official Basem Naim said.
He told Reuters that Izzeldeen al-Hayya and his family had survived a dawn airstrike. Hamas sources said several people, including Hayya's daughter-in-law, had been wounded but there were no deaths.
The Israeli military had no immediate comment.
Naim described Izzeldeen al-Hayya, born in 1997, as the Hamas chief's last surviving son, with four others having been killed by Israeli forces.
The family of one of the late sons survived Friday's strike, Naim said.
Hamas said in a statement that the Israeli military had targeted a residential apartment, linking the attack to threats made by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz against Hayya.
Hamas accused Israel of seeking to undermine a 2025 Gaza ceasefire agreement and said Israel bore full responsibility for the consequences of its continued attacks.
Izzeldeen is the twin brother of Hamam Khalil al-Hayya, who was killed in a 2025 Israeli airstrike targeting Hamas leaders in Qatar, Naim said.
Named Hamas' overall leader in July, Hayya narrowly escaped assassination himself in the Qatar strike.
Hayya warned of possible retaliation on Thursday after Israeli attacks killed at least 10 people in Gaza.
Two separate Israeli strikes killed five Palestinians in Gaza on Friday, medics said.

The first strike killed three Palestinians and wounded two in the city of Rafah, medical sources told Reuters. The Israeli military spokesperson said the military had struck three fighters without giving further information.
In the second attack, Palestinian medics said two people who worked as civil guards at an office of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Gaza City were killed.
There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military or MSF, and Reuters could not immediately authenticate whether the two worked for MSF.

Israel has continued to carry out attacks it says target Hamas, but the attacks have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by US President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament.
At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli troops control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, while Hamas controls a narrow strip of territory along Gaza's coast.

Israel's assault on Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians since 2023, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced the territory's entire population and led to assessments of genocide by scholars and a United Nations inquiry.
Israel has denied the allegations of genocide, saying it acted in self-defence after Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an attack on Israel in October 2023.

7d8c221dd647316c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Despite nearly three in four Malaysian adults expressing confidence in their ability to recognise scams, seven in 10 who encounter a scam attempt still interact with it, highlighting a gap between perceived awareness and actual vulnerability, a report found.

Nonprofit network Global Anti-Scam Alliance, which combats online scams and fraud through research, intelligence sharing and cross-sector collaboration, said its latest survey revealed a gap between confidence and reality, noting that Malaysians’ confidence in recognising scams does not necessarily translate into safer behaviour.

The report also found that 83 per cent of Malaysian adults had encountered a scam in 2026, a figure largely unchanged from the previous year, with phone calls remaining the most common channel through which scams were encountered at 69 per cent.
It also highlighted that one in seven Malaysian parents (14 per cent) said their children aged seven to 17 had experienced at least one scam.
“Scam-recognition confidence in Malaysia skews strongly toward Millennials and Gen X (76 per cent and 78 per cent respectively) and men (75 per cent).
“By comparison, a lack of confidence is much higher among those from the Boomer generation (34 per cent), those aged 55+ (25 per cent) and women (20 per cent),” it said.

The State of Scams in Malaysia 2026 report surveyed 1,930 Malaysian adults aged 18 and above between March 16 and April 13 this year, examining how scams reach the public, how people respond to them, and their financial and emotional impact on those affected.

The report also highlighted the financial consequences of engaging with scam attempts, finding that three in 10 of those who interacted with scammers lost money, either by making payments, divulging personal information or both.
Investment and impersonation scams recorded high interaction rates, with 63 per cent and 65 per cent of participants respectively reporting encounters with such attempts.
WhatsApp and Telegram were the most commonly cited platforms for scam encounters, with 67 per cent and 40 per cent of respondents respectively reporting encounters on the messaging apps.
“Overall, 76 per cent of scam attempts in the past 12 months took place on platforms with direct messaging functions,” it said.
Scam prevention
Despite the high number of scam encounters, the report found that public awareness and vigilance played an important role in preventing people from becoming victims.
It said the most common reasons Malaysians gave for avoiding scam attempts were that the messages did not seem legitimate (45 per cent) or appeared too good to be true (43 per cent).
Other reasons included being educated on warning signs (41 per cent) and having a general rule of not responding to unsolicited messages or calls (40 per cent).

“Similar intuitive reasons were cited for why scam interactions did not result in financial or personal data losses, with 39 per cent saying the offers appeared too good to be true, while 37 per cent found requests for money suspicious,” it said.

The report also found that public awareness campaigns and advertisements were the most commonly cited sources of information helping Malaysian adults recognise and avoid scams, with half of all respondents identifying them as useful.

“Public awareness campaigns are the most commonly cited source of scam prevention education in Malaysia, suggesting government and public-sector efforts are helping consumers recognise and avoid scams.

“This aligns with wider perceptions that government and consumer support organisations are performing relatively well in the fight against scams, though online platforms are viewed as falling short of expectations,” it said.
Still, nearly three in 10 Malaysian adults believe public service organisations, including the government and police, bear the primary responsibility for protecting them from scams.
“The police lead in scam prevention and resolution, particularly through education (62 per cent), ease of reporting (58 per cent) and enforcement (55 per cent),” it said.

Regarding the role of financial institutions, nearly half of Malaysian adults (45 per cent) believe banks should always reimburse scam victims, while 78 per cent support banks blocking transactions above a certain value if they suspect the transactions are linked to a scam.

22d9f6afa5fd7004: BANGUI (Central African Republic), Nov 28 — With a vodka or a beer in hand, young Central Africans watch a football match in “Moscow”, a Russian-run bar in the capital, Bangui.
On some bottles is printed “Made in the Central African Republic with Russian technology” in Sango, one of the country’s two official languages.
The Central African Republic is one of the world’s poorest countries and the last bastion of the Russian paramilitary Wagner Group once led by the late Yevgeny Prigozhin.
Elsewhere on the continent, it is gradually being replaced by the Africa Corps, which reports directly to the defence ministry in Moscow.
On the streets of Bangui, it is not uncommon to come across Russians in uniforms, their faces hidden and with weapons on their belts.
Outside restaurants and supermarkets, their camouflaged vehicles stand out and are so recognisable that all cars stop quickly to give way to them.
Sachets of vodka

Deployed in 2018 at the request of President Faustin-Archange Touadéra to support the Central African army, Wagner fighters have become the government’s main security partners in exchange for lucrative contracts in the gold and diamond sectors.
The group is now diversifying and strengthening its presence by establishing itself in drinks manufacturing and distribution.
Russian water, soda, beer and vodka are made locally and sold at significantly lower prices than those of the competition.
Street vendors even sell 50-millilitre sachets of coconut-flavoured vodka for 150 CFA francs (RM1.03).
“They seek to conquer the smallest possible spaces. They are the only competitors of the Castel group,” Central African researcher Soleil-Parfait Kalessopo told AFP.
The Mocaf brewery, a subsidiary of the French group Castel, has been in the Central African Republic since 1953, and had a monopoly on the alcohol market before the Russians arrived.
Castel did not provide any figures on its production in the country when asked by AFP.
In March 2023, one of its factories was set on fire by four masked men dressed like Wagner mercenaries, according to security camera footage, which showed them throwing Molotov cocktails.
“The events of 2023 are now behind us,” the Castel group said, when asked about its performance since the arrival of Russian competitors.
At the head of the First Industrial Company, which markets drinks produced by the Russians, is Dmitry Sytyi, according to Jeune Afrique magazine.
Sytyi is also director of the Russian House in Bangui, and is described by the All Eyes on Wagner collective as “one of the pillars of the Wagner network” in Central Africa.
‘Danger for democracy’
The Russian House, opened in 2021, offers many free cultural and sporting activities to people in Bangui, as well as Russian language lessons.
Every afternoon, children play on the roundabout, trampolines and swings in the garden to the sound of a promotional video for Russia.
In front of the cultural centre, along the Ubangi river, stands a statue of Prigozhin, who was killed when a private plane crashed in 2023, two months after his aborted mutiny in Russia.
Another symbol of the Russian presence is a fresco at a market showing President Vladimir Putin shaking hands with Touadéra.
Most Central Africans appear to fear the Russians, refusing to mention their existence for fear of reprisals.
“They have methods of repression, of operating, which really terrorise the population,” said Kalessopo.
Several human rights groups have accused Wagner paramilitaries of serious abuses, notably torture and murder, in several countries, including the Central African Republic.

For lawyer Crépin Mboli-Goumba, a member of the opposition Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution (BRDC), Wagner fighters represent “a danger for democrats and democracy” by their involvement in the economy and politics.
Blurred lines

As in Mali, where the Africa Corps has supplanted Wagner, Moscow has looked to impose its new structure on the Central African authorities, although not without resistance from Touadéra, whose personal security has relied on the group for several years.
A Central African minister confirmed to AFP that the Africa Corps was in the country but the subject remains sensitive.
“There was an agreement, they are here with the others,” said Pascal Bida Koyagbele, a minister in charge of major public works and a close ally of the president.
Wagner operatives, he added, have “the advantage of knowing the terrain” and “generally guide the Africa Corps personnel”.
Asked about the matter, communications minister Evariste Ngamana sidestepped the question. “Wagner or Africa Corps, it makes no difference. Ask the Russians. It’s an internal issue,” he said.
The arrival of the Africa Corps has not ousted Wagner from the Central African Republic.
The development of “military-technical cooperation” with Africa Corps “would not, in itself, constitute a replacement for the Wagner Corps”, said Russian military expert Sergey Eledinov.
But the blurred lines could become “a factor of destabilisation”, warned Anicet-Georges Dologuele, a Central African former prime minister now in opposition.
Touadéra has taken significant risks, he said, adding: “I don’t know many human beings who would dare to disobey President Putin.” — AFP
f8502129c84f6235: KYOTO, Nov 28 — Visitors from Japan and overseas marvelled at the brilliant reds and yellows of Kyoto’s autumn foliage season, as it transformed the city’s temples, gardens and mountains with a blaze of colour.

The ancient Japanese capital is known for its cherry blossoms in spring, but autumn is another peak tourism season, particularly for local visitors keen to enjoy the centuries-old tradition of viewing vibrant fall foliage.
“The autumn leaves themselves are beautiful,” Rie Segawa, 34-year-old visitor from Osaka, told AFP, adding that the colours make her “feel calm”.
“Seeing them turn red makes me happy to see the seasons changing,” she said.
Anthony Piglioni from France said he’d heard so much about the famous cherry blossom season but “the colours are just as beautiful as in the spring”.
“It’s incredible... the colours, the landscapes... very zen, very relaxing,” the 37-year-old told AFP.
Kyoto has a long-standing tradition of appreciating autumn foliage.

During the Heian period between the late eighth century and the late 12th century, when the city was Japan’s capital, looking at autumn leaves was an important seasonal pastime among the aristocracy, much like cherry blossom viewing in spring.
The aristocracy would visit the mountains and compose poems celebrating the beauty of the autumn colours.
Over time, trees such as Japanese maples were planted in aristocratic residences, temples and gardens across Kyoto.
Scientists say climate change is delaying famed autumn foliage season in Japan, pushing back the peak display of red and yellow leaves, although this year was within the normal range for Kyoto. — AFP
f1bca8dab2d3987a: PARIS, Nov 28 — Far-right leader Marine Le Pen is frontrunner in the race to become the next French president, but analysts say a fragmented field and a volatile electorate make the outcome far less certain than current polls suggest

Five months before the vote, more than 30 declared or potential candidates are competing to succeed President Emmanuel Macron as the country heads into one of its most consequential votes in an unusually tense social climate.

The public is angry over the rising cost of living and eager for change, with many blaming Macron for the country’s troubles after nearly a decade in power. Protests in October descended into some of the worst rioting in years.
But the government is under pressure from markets and the European Union to rein in spending.
“There is huge potential for volatility over the coming five months,” said Jeremy Cliffe, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations.
“The range of candidates is in rapid flux. The French economy is fragile and the chances of a market shock are real. Recent protests add another element of unpredictability.”
Testing the waters
Sophie Meunier, director of the EU Program at Princeton, said the campaign had not begun in earnest.
“Several uncertainties could upend the race,” she said.
Le Pen, who ran for president in the 2012, 2017 and 2022 elections, is in her strongest position yet and dominates opinion polls for the first round.

The National Rally (RN) candidate is running despite an embezzlement conviction over a fake jobs scam in European Parliament, after an appeals court in July shortened a ban from office against her. France’s highest court is to decide whether to uphold that verdict early next year.
Opinion polls suggest she could face hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon of the France Unbowed (LFI) party in the second round.
The crowded field in the centre and on the right has raised fears voters could face a choice between two extremes.

Former prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal have been campaigning for months, Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner has made a surprise entry into the race and little-known mayor of Cannes David Lisnard has surged in the polls.

There is no unity on the left either. Centre-left candidate Raphael Glucksmann has positioned himself as an alternative to Mélenchon, criticising Green leader Marine Tondelier’s willingness to work with the hard-left veteran.
But analysts say candidates are still testing the waters, with future alliances possible.
“A lot of people will drop out,” said Damien Bol, a professor of political science at Sciences Po university.
The uncertainty reflects a broader shift in French politics, which was once dominated by strong parties but has become increasingly candidate-driven.
“A majority of French people just don’t know who to vote for,” said Bol.
“The only kind of support base that is not volatile is actually the support base of Marine Le Pen.”
Change over stability
Erwan Lestrohan of the Odoxa polling organisation said one in two French voters would rather the country’s next president were not one of those currently running.
“The distinctive feature of this presidential election is that no candidate enjoys the support of a majority of French voters,” he said.
Meunier said most French people wanted change rather than stability.
“This is the worst possible environment for a continuity candidate, especially given the absence of an incumbent and the fragmentation of the centrist bloc,” she said.
To win in the current conditions, Le Pen does not necessarily need to expand her support further, she said.
“It may be enough for her opponents to remain divided,” Meunier said.
Mélenchon, whose LFI party has backed the recent protests, has also emerged as a strong contender by tapping into anti-establishment sentiment.
“He is offering a confidently left-wing programme that places his candidacy on the side of ‘the people’,” said Cliffe.
Philippe, once billed as the centrist camp’s best chance of defeating Le Pen, has been slipping in the polls, with some describing his campaign as lacklustre.
He was overtaken by Lisnard, who has taken social media by storm, in a Toluna Harris Interactive opinion poll published on Monday.
While pressure has been growing on the centrists to conduct a primary, Philippe has ruled out taking part.
Mathieu Gallard, research director at the Ipsos polling institute, say France’s squabbling centrists could still get their act together, although it was unclear who the consensus candidate might be.
“Voters in the centrist camp are unlikely to enjoy the prospect of a Le Pen-Mélenchon runoff.” — AFP
c824cc7cdafc7b78: MADRID, Nov 28 — No coach in the history of Spanish football has won more La Liga matches than Atletico Madrid’s Diego Simeone.
The Argentine claimed his 345th league victory last weekend to keep the Rojiblancos in the race to chase down Spain’s traditional giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid.
Third-placed Atletico visit Elche on Saturday with Simeone looking to keep adding to his record and deliver a third La Liga title, adding to his conquests in 2014 and 2021.
Atletico trail leaders Barcelona by five points before they face the Catalans on December 2, in a match brought forward because of the teams’ participation in the Spanish Super Cup in January.
Barcelona visit Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday, while Real Madrid, second and two points ahead of Atletico, host Alaves on Saturday.
Simeone surpassed the late Luis Aragones, on 344 league victories, to stand alone at the top of the all-time list.
“I would like to share this number with all the people behind these 345 victories,” said Simeone, speaking of his family, current and former staff and players.
“I don’t usually get excited about many things, but getting to this point has taken incredible work.”
Prying two league titles away from giants Real Madrid and Barcelona was an impressive achievement, and Atletico have shown this season they have the tools to do it again.
Until their defeat by Barcelona before the international break, Atletico won their seven prior league matches, including a derby victory over Real Madrid.
Their strong start has come without star player Julian Alvarez being at his best, which shows they can still find a higher gear.
The Argentine forward wanted to leave in the summer and tried to force through a move to Barcelona, but Atletico staunchly resisted.
Alvarez started the season at a low ebb and struggling for fitness, and has scored just three goals across all competitions to date.
However the 2022 World Cup winner has started to show some of his quality in recent appearances and tensions with the supporters have eased.
‘Same ambition, hunger
Alvarez set up Atletico’s first two goals against Getafe in their win last weekend and scored with a free-kick against Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday.
“He’s truly an incredible player, fantastic. I like him as a person, I’ll support him as a footballer, I understand him as a player,” said Simeone on Wednesday.

“Even though he hasn’t scored in previous matches, there isn’t an attacking move that doesn’t go through him, and he always contributes important things. To get where we want to be, we need the best Julian Alvarez.”
Simeone’s other two title successes were powered by goals from South American strikers, with Brazilian Diego Costa key in 2014, and Uruguay’s Luis Suarez vital in 2021.
A resurgent Alvarez would help Atletico’s bid for a third crown under Simeone.
Atletico midfielder Koke said Simeone has not changed since arriving at the club in 2011, even though his football has become more progressive in recent years.
“I think practically nothing has changed, because he still has the same drive, the same ambition, the same hunger, and I think that will never change,” said the veteran midfielder.

“Obviously, he’s a bit older but everything else remains the same... he’s still very demanding in training, he doesn’t let us relax for a second, and that’s what makes the difference and allows us to compete against the best.” — AFP
9c04dfa0fc0222e8: From Moaz Nair
Whenever political temperatures rise, the same old script is replayed: DAP is a threat to the position of the Malays and the sanctity of Islam.

However, if we set aside emotional sentiment and evaluate the situation based on demographic realities, the Federal Constitution, and the latest 2027 budget, this narrative is clearly more of a political gimmick than fact.
Logically speaking, how could a party often labelled a "Chinese party" possibly seize absolute power in this country?

The Chinese community makes up only about 20% of the total citizenry in Malaysia, and not all of them vote for DAP. With numbers this small, it is impossible for any Chinese-dominated party to form a government on its own, let alone alter the fundamental structure of the nation.

More importantly, the pillars of national power remain firmly in Malay hands. From the institution of the Malay rulers and the office of the prime minister, right down to the top leadership of the civil service, the armed forces and police, all are led by Malays.
Fears that Malay political power will be eroded are simply manufactured anxieties.
Respecting the constitution and social contract
The track record since the formation of the unity government proves that DAP respects the Federal Constitution.

As acknowledged by Umno leaders themselves, DAP leaders have never questioned Article 153 regarding the special position of the Malays and Bumiputeras, the status of Islam as the religion of the federation, or Bahasa Melayu as the national language.
In fact, when the government organised the Bumiputera Economic Congress to strengthen the Malay economic agenda, DAP voiced no objections.
This proves the party supports efforts to empower Islam and the Bumiputera economy, so long as they operate within the constitutional framework without denying the rights of other races.
Latest proof in the 2027 budget
Anti-Islam accusations also flatly contradict the government allocations approved alongside DAP cabinet ministers.
In the 2027 federal budget, allocations for Islamic affairs are not only untouched, they surge to RM3.1 billion compared to RM2.6 billion previously.

This substantial funding covers full Socso contributions for 40,000 mosque officials and takmir teachers, special incentives for Kafa teachers, as well as the establishment of the Malaysian Pondok and Turath Advisory Council.
In Penang, which has been led by DAP since 2008, the Malay community and Islamic institutions continue to be empowered.

Through the 2027 state budget, chief minister Chow Kon Yeow’s administration is fully funding the construction of three new mosques worth RM14 million (in addition to a RM3.9 million contribution for Masjid Cherok Tok Kun Atas), allocating RM15.07 million to build three Sekolah Agama Rakyat, and channelling one-off special aid to Kafa, tahfiz, and pondok teachers.
Furthermore, DAP-elected representatives nationwide continue to actively serve the Malay communities in their respective constituencies regardless of background.
Exemplary DAP ministerial performance

Rather than pursuing any racial agenda, DAP ministers have built a strong reputation for administrative competence and tangible delivery that directly benefits all Malaysians - the majority of whom are Malay and Bumiputera.
At the transport ministry, Loke Siew Fook earned widespread praise for a no-nonsense, data-driven approach to fixing public infrastructure.

He enforced strict reliability targets that significantly reduced LRT breakdowns, digitalised road tax and licence renewals via the MyJPJ app to eliminate long queues, cracked down on overloaded lorries to make highways safer, and kept major projects like the East Coast Rail Link and Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS Link firmly on track.

Meanwhile, since taking over the Federal Territories portfolio in December 2025, Hannah Yeoh - the first Kuala Lumpur MP to hold the post in two decades - has delivered immediate, practical relief to urban residents.

She halved DBKL rental rates for over 10,000 petty traders, lowered Ramadan bazaar site fees to RM400, channelled RM300 million into upgrading all 51 public housing areas, gazetted over 550 permanent green spaces, and rolled out 13 governance reforms to break tender cartels and tighten anti-corruption oversight.

Similarly, under housing and local government minister Nga Kor Ming, Malaysia surpassed its target of building 500,000 affordable homes, revived over 1,500 abandoned housing projects to rescue around 176,000 homebuyers, and completed more than 15,000 public infrastructure upgrades nationwide.
Across the board, DAP ministers have focused squarely on modernising public services and uplifting communities across all races.
Not a single race party

It is often forgotten that DAP is not an exclusive club for one race. The party’s membership and leadership include many Malaysians of Malay, Indian, and Orang Asli descent, as well as the indigenous peoples of Sabah and Sarawak.
Today, DAP leaders and ministers are focused on their core duties - driving the economy and solving the people’s problems - which ultimately uplifts all races.
Critics often claim the current government is subservient to DAP because the party holds a large number of parliamentary seats within Pakatan Harapan.
However, if there is truly any hidden agenda to undermine Islam or the Malays, prove it through legal channels and the courts, rather than relying on rhetoric on the ceramah stage.

Malaysians deserve a more mature brand of politics. It is high time we judge any political party based on its work performance and tangible contributions to the nation, rather than falling into the trap of the politics of fear deliberately stoked for the narrow interests of a few.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
dc878bee4701727a: Setiap kali suhu politik meningkat, skrip lama pasti diulang: DAP didakwa menjadi ancaman kepada kedudukan orang Melayu dan kesucian agama Islam.

Namun, jika kita ketepikan sentimen emosi dan menilai berdasarkan realiti demografi, Perlembagaan Persekutuan, serta rekod Belanjawan 2027 yang terkini, naratif ini jelas lebih bersifat gimik politik berbanding fakta.
Matematik demografi yang mudah
Secara logik akal, bagaimana sebuah parti yang sering dilabel sebagai ‘parti Cina’ mampu merampas kuasa mutlak di negara ini?

Populasi masyarakat Cina di Malaysia hanya sekitar 20% daripada keseluruhan rakyat—dan bukan kesemuanya mengundi DAP. Dengan angka sekecil ini, adalah mustahil untuk mana-mana parti yang didominasi satu kaum membentuk kerajaan bersendirian, apatah lagi mengubah struktur asas negara.

Lebih penting, tunjang kuasa negara kekal utuh di tangan orang Melayu. Bermula daripada institusi raja-raja Melayu dan jawatan perdana menteri, sehinggalah ke peneraju tertinggi perkhidmatan awam, Angkatan Tentera Malaysia (ATM) dan Polis Diraja Malaysia (PDRM), semuanya diterajui oleh orang Melayu. Kebimbangan kononnya kuasa Melayu akan terhakis hanyalah ketakutan yang direka-reka.
Hormat Perlembagaan dan kontrak sosial
Rekod sejak penubuhan kerajaan perpaduan membuktikan DAP menghormati Perlembagaan Persekutuan.

Seperti yang diakui sendiri oleh pimpinan Umno, pemimpin DAP tidak pernah mempersoalkan Perkara 153 berhubung hak istimewa orang Melayu dan Bumiputera, kedudukan Islam sebagai agama persekutuan, mahupun bahasa Melayu sebagai bahasa kebangsaan.

Malah, apabila kerajaan menganjurkan Kongres Ekonomi Bumiputera untuk memperkukuh agenda ekonomi Melayu, tiada bantahan disuarakan oleh DAP. Ini membuktikan parti itu menyokong usaha memperkasakan syiar Islam dan ekonomi Bumiputera, selagi ia berjalan dalam kerangka Perlembagaan tanpa menafikan hak kaum lain.
Bukti terkini dalam Belanjawan 2027
Tuduhan anti-Islam juga bercanggah sama sekali dengan angka peruntukan kerajaan yang diluluskan bersama jemaah menteri DAP.

Dalam Belanjawan 2027 di peringkat persekutuan, peruntukan hal ehwal Islam bukan sahaja tidak dikurangkan, malah melonjak kepada RM3.1 bilion berbanding RM2.6 bilion sebelumnya. Dana besar ini merangkumi caruman penuh Perkeso untuk 40,000 petugas masjid dan guru takmir, insentif khas guru Kafa, serta penubuhan Majlis Penasihat Pondok dan Turath Malaysia.

Di Pulau Pinang yang diterajui DAP sejak 2008 pula, masyarakat Melayu dan institusi Islam terus diperkasa. Menerusi Belanjawan Negeri 2027, pentadbiran Ketua Menteri Chow Kon Yeow membiayai sepenuhnya pembinaan tiga masjid baharu bernilai RM14 juta (selain sumbangan RM3.9 juta untuk Masjid Cherok Tok Kun Atas), memperuntukkan RM15.07 juta bagi membina tiga Sekolah Agama Rakyat (SAR), serta menyalurkan bantuan khas sekali beri kepada guru Kafa, tahfiz, dan pondok.
Di samping itu, wakil rakyat DAP di seluruh negara terus aktif menyantuni komuniti Melayu di kawasan masing-masing tanpa mengira latar belakang.
Prestasi cemerlang menteri DAP

Daripada mengejar sebarang agenda perkauman, menteri-menteri DAP membina reputasi kukuh menerusi kecekapan pentadbiran dan penyampaian nyata yang memberi manfaat langsung kepada rakyat biasa—yang majoritinya terdiri daripada orang Melayu dan Bumiputera.

Di Kementerian Pengangkutan, Loke Siew Fook meraih pujian meluas atas pendekatan tegas dan berasaskan data dalam membaiki infrastruktur awam. Beliau menguatkuasakan sasaran kebolehpercayaan ketat yang berjaya mengurangkan gangguan perkhidmatan LRT secara ketara, mendigitalkan pembaharuan cukai jalan dan lesen melalui aplikasi MyJPJ bagi menghapuskan barisan panjang, bertindak tegas terhadap lori lebih muatan demi keselamatan lebuh raya, serta memastikan projek utama seperti Laluan Rel Pantai Timur (ECRL) dan Sistem Transit Rapid (RTS) Johor Bahru–Singapura berjalan mengikut jadual.

Sementara itu, sejak menerajui portfolio Wilayah Persekutuan pada Disember 2025, Hannah Yeoh—Ahli Parlimen Kuala Lumpur pertama memegang jawatan itu dalam tempoh dua dekad—telah membawa kelegaan segera dan praktikal kepada warga kota. Beliau memotong separuh kadar sewa tapak penjaja DBKL untuk lebih 10,000 peniaga kecil, menurunkan kadar tapak bazar Ramadan kepada RM400, menyalurkan RM300 juta bagi menaik taraf semua 51 kawasan perumahan awam (PA dan PPR), mewartakan lebih 550 kawasan lapang hijau kekal, serta memperkenalkan 13 pembaharuan tadbir urus bagi memecahkan kartel tender dan memperketat pengawasan antirasuah.

Begitu juga di bawah Menteri Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan Nga Kor Ming, Malaysia berjaya melepasi sasaran membina 500,000 rumah mampu milik, memulihkan lebih 1,500 projek perumahan terbengkalai yang menyelamatkan sekitar 176,000 pembeli rumah, serta menyiapkan lebih 15,000 projek naik taraf infrastruktur awam di seluruh negara. Secara keseluruhannya, menteri-menteri DAP memberi tumpuan penuh kepada usaha memodenkan perkhidmatan awam dan membela komuniti merentas semua kaum.
Bukan parti satu kaum

Sering kali dilupakan, DAP bukanlah kelab eksklusif untuk satu bangsa. Keahlian dan barisan kepimpinan parti ini turut disertai oleh ramai rakyat Malaysia berbangsa Melayu, India, Orang Asli, serta pribumi Sabah dan Sarawak.
Hari ini, pemimpin dan menteri daripada DAP memfokuskan tugas hakiki mereka—memacu ekonomi dan menyelesaikan masalah rakyat—yang akhirnya mengangkat martabat semua kaum.
Kesimpulan

734bdd863b2bef95: SUNGAI SIPUT: The passing of Bisnumaya Thapa on Nov 22 at age 96 marks the end of a remarkable chapter in the history of the Nepali community in Malaysia.

Believed to have been the oldest Nepali residing in Malaysia, Bisnumaya belonged to a generation whose lives were profoundly shaped by World War II, British colonial rule and the struggles that preceded the birth of an independent Malaya.
Her life was not merely a story of longevity but one of migration, courage, sacrifice and motherhood. She leaves behind seven daughters and their spouses, 23 grandchildren and 27 great-grandchildren.

Born in 1930 at a military camp in Dehradun, India to a Gurkha soldier whose family hailed from Pokhara in Nepal, Bisnumaya grew up steeped in the Gurkha traditions of courage, discipline and loyalty.

Her husband, the late Bal Bahadur Thapa, was also a Gurkha soldier whose military service began during WWII. Surviving military records reveal that he served with the 4th Burma Regiment and attained the rank of lance corporal.

His certificate records his participation in the Second Burma Campaign and lists the 1939-1945 Star among his military honours. He was discharged in May 1952, with his military character officially assessed as “very good”.
Bal’s commitment to service continued in Malaya, where he joined the Police Field Force in August 1952 and served as a corporal until Oct 1956, amidst the Malayan Emergency.
While her husband’s contributions were recorded in military and police documents, Bisnumaya’s own sacrifices went largely undocumented. But they were no less significant.

Settling in Heawood Estate in Sungai Siput, Perak, she witnessed Malaya’s independence in 1957 and the formation of Malaysia in 1963. Her adopted country became the home upon which generations of her family would build their futures.
The strength of a mother

The most defining chapter of Bisnumaya’s life began in 1975, when her husband passed away. At 45, she found herself raising seven daughters far from her ancestral homeland, without extended family or friends she could depend on.
Her eldest daughter was 20; her youngest just four. Despite her limited command of the local language and lack of support, she refused to allow her circumstances to determine her children’s future.
Through perseverance, sacrifice and a strong belief in education, she dedicated herself to giving her daughters the best possible upbringing and opportunities.

For Bisnumaya, education was about more than securing employment or financial independence: it was also about developing character and instilling values such as integrity, humility, discipline and respect for others.

Throughout her life, Bisnumaya remained a proud custodian of her family’s Gurkha heritage, recounting stories of soldiers’ courage and sacrifices during the Japanese occupation and subsequent communist insurgency in Malaya.

One of her cherished dreams was to see a member of her family follow in her late husband’s footsteps by serving in the military or police force. That dream was fulfilled through her grandson, S Shankar, who attained the rank of assistant commissioner of police.
For Bisnumaya, this symbolised the continuation of a family tradition of duty and service, connecting pre-independence Malaya with modern Malaysia.

Her other grandchildren have also distinguished themselves in various fields in Malaysia and Singapore. Their achievements include doctorates in atmospheric science at the University of Cambridge and virology at Universiti Malaya, as well as careers in healthcare, public service and the private sector.
Despite spending most of her life in Malaysia, Bisnumaya remained deeply committed to preserving her Nepali identity, emphasising customs and traditions, family unity and respect for elders.
Culture, for her, was not merely expressed through ceremonies or celebrations; it was a way of life, reflected in one’s conduct, relationships and responsibilities towards family and community.
Even in her final farewell, these principles remained evident. Her funeral was rich in Nepali traditions, reflecting the heritage she had passed on to her descendants.
Bisnumaya’s nearly century-long life served as a bridge between Nepal and Malaysia, encompassing an increasingly distant and largely undocumented chapter of Malaysian history.
She will be remembered not simply for the 96 years she lived, but for the generations she shaped, the history she carried and the culture she preserved.

Her story reminds us that the making of a nation is not solely the work of those whose names appear in history books, but also of ordinary individuals whose extraordinary sacrifices help shape its future.
77ad897d0a285c54: LONDON: Southampton beat spygate rivals Middlesbrough 2-0 on Friday in the first meeting between the feuding clubs since the scandal that rocked the Championship last season.
The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-off final last season after being caught spying on a Middlesbrough training session.
Southampton admitted sending an analyst to film from a bush before the first leg of their play-off semi-final win against Middlesbrough.
They also spied on Ipswich and Oxford prior to second tier matches last season.

Southampton's removal from the play-off final against Hull cost them the chance to win a lucrative promotion to the Premier League, with the Tigers beating Middlesbrough to secure their place in the top-flight.
The plot was masterminded by Southampton manager Tonda Eckert, who was given a suspended six-week ban, running until the end of the 2027-28 season, for his role in the scandal.

Middlesbrough have climbed to the top of the Championship this season, while Southampton, who started the season with a four-point deduction for their cheating, are also chasing an automatic promotion place.
It was Southampton who took the spoils on a freezing night when feelings were still running hot at St Mary's, with 10 players booked across the two teams.
Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz scored Southampton's goals in the second half to lift them into sixth place, four points behind Middlesbrough.
"One of the best games the Championship could produce. There were moments that could go in both directions and I think over 90 minutes we deserved to win," Eckert said.
"This game brings emotions and you need to use them to your advantage.
"I am grateful to our club, to the supporters. The club had every right to make a different decision after Spygate.
"The reality is we started on minus four and we are still playing catch up."
Former Middlesbrough forward Azaz rubbed salt into his old club's wounds by celebrating in front of their travelling fans, making a crying gesture.
Middlesbrough were booed off the pitch by Southampton fans at full-time as "Stop crying your heart out" by Oasis was played over the tannoy.
Summing up the seething enmity between the clubs, Azaz said "none whatsoever" when asked if he had any regrets over his celebration.
"They sang about my family home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back," he said.

1dc118535c0d80ac: MEXICO CITY: Mexico's recent string of cartel kingpin takedowns, aided by US intelligence, suggests closer cooperation with Washington as President Claudia Sheinbaum comes under pressure to advance the so-called war on drugs.

A swarm of heavily armed helicopters involved in the arrest of cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza — alias "Chapo Isidro", one of the FBI's 10 most wanted men — served as a reminder of that ever-closer relationship last Saturday.

It also marks leftist Sheinbaum's move away from the "Hugs, not bullets" policy of her predecessor, Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, which avoided direct confrontation with Mexico's drug-trafficking cartels.
Unlike Sheinbaum, the previous administration also avoided acknowledging such cooperation with the United States.
Mexican officials "have been very cooperative, way more cooperative than the last administration", US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told Congress in June.
Sheinbaum has set conditions, however.
While US intelligence is welcome, foreign agents on Mexican soil — as President Donald Trump has proposed — are not.
"The Mexicans have done more than they've ever done before to go after these groups, but it is still not nearly enough," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in September.
Trump has threatened to conduct strikes on cartels if the Mexican government itself fails to act.
WHAT ABOUT POLITICS?
US-Mexico cooperation is "contradictory", according to national security expert Raul Benitez Manaut.
"Mexico cooperates extensively in capturing, imprisoning, investigating narcos... but not narcopoliticians," he told AFP.
In April, Washington accused then-governor of Sinaloa, Ruben Rocha Moya, of links to the drug trade.
Rocha, a member of ruling party Morena, left office but has not been prosecuted, with Sheinbaum insisting there is no evidence to arrest him.
The government's Operation Swarm has arrested more than 100 public officials, targeting politicians linked to criminal groups. All are municipal-level officials.
Sheinbaum's own Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch says cartels have been able to act "with impunity because there were authorities who allowed themselves to be corrupted".
LIKE IN HOLLYWOOD
The capture of Chapo Isidro last Saturday was a flashy operation designed to capture the world's attention.
A video published by the army shows armed soldiers entering the kingpin's home at night, later depicting him handcuffed on a couch.
His arrest triggered retaliation in the form of burnt-out vehicles blocking roads in Sinaloa, which also suffered multiple shootouts.
Twenty people died that night: four soldiers and 16 alleged criminals.

Mexico asked Washington to help "so that we could have more intelligence", Sheinbaum told a press conference, adding that she had authorised US drones to enter Mexican territory, locate the target and strike.
'GOOD FRIEND'

The US has also provided intelligence in recent operations against the notorious Jalisco New Generation Cartel, including one that led to the death of its leader, Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera, in February.

Mexico has consistently expressed gratitude for the information-sharing, while US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) chief Terry Cole has described Garcia Harfuch as a "trusted partner and a good friend of the United States".
"He knows the importance of sharing intelligence (and) targeting criminals," Cole told a press conference in Buenos Aires.
The DEA, however, rankled Mexico by opening a direct tip line for reports related to the Sinaloa cartel, a move Sheinbaum described as "interference".
The Mexican leader had already protested the presence of two CIA agents in an anti-drug operation in her country, which only came to light after they died in a traffic accident.
AN UNSOLVABLE PROBLEM

During Lopez Obrador's six-year term, army clashes with criminal gangs resulted in the deaths of 210 "assailants" every year, compared with 321 deaths in 2025 alone under Sheinbaum, official figures show.
Arrests by the armed forces also doubled under the current government, rising from 7,230 in 2023 to 18,138 in 2025.
But the drug business isn't going anywhere.

"The more you behead organisations that in turn are not dismantled in terms of their assets... what happens is that they fragment," Ernesto Lopez Portillo, a professor at the Ibero-American University, told AFP.
"The market is fought over by an increasing number of organisations that use violence," he said.

59b72c4fa671f33f: PARIS: Paris FC missed the opportunity to join capital rivals Paris Saint-Germain at the top of Ligue 1 as they lost 1-0 on Friday at Brest, with Luck Zogbe's solitary goal instead firing the Brittany team into the Champions League places.

Liam Rosenior's Paris FC, backed by the billionaire Arnault family, have big ambitions and knew a fourth consecutive Ligue 1 win would allow them to go level with neighbours PSG at the top of the standings.

But their winning streak came to an end as Egil Selvik performed heroics in the Brest goal, allowing the home side -- who had to deal with the tragic death of coach Eric Roy during the close season -- to claim a fourth victory on the bounce that lifts them up to the giddy heights of third.
"Four clean sheets in a row and we defend like hell, so it's a great feeling," goalkeeper Selvik told broadcaster Ligue 1+.
"We can be proud but we still have to continue the work. It's a long season but we are happy.”

Paris FC therefore remain three points behind Luis Enrique's PSG, who can extend their advantage at the top with a win at home to Lorient on Saturday. Brest climb above Lille, Lyon and Marseille and are two points behind Paris FC.

Brest went ahead midway through the first half when a Ludovic Ajorque effort came back off the post and the ball rebounded out to Zogbe, the young Ivorian full-back converting for his first senior goal.
Selvik then saved superbly to keep out a header from Ligue 1's leading scorer Lassine Sinayoko, the first of a remarkable eight saves made on the night by the Norwegian international goalkeeper.
He denied Sinayoko again at the start of the second half, with Rudy Matondo hitting the follow-up off the crossbar.
Selvik, signed in the close season from English second-tier outfit Watford, intervened time and time again to frustrate the visitors, as he kept a fourth straight clean sheet.

The last time Brest won four successive Ligue 1 matches was three years ago under Roy, during the 2023/24 season in which they finished third to qualify for the Champions League for the first time in their history.
380dd78efd0487af: LONDON: Britain's Princess Catherine is seen brushing away tears in a new documentary about her cancer journey as she listens to messages of support from her three children.

Catherine, 44, who is married to heir to the throne Prince William, was filmed for the highly personal documentary taking part in one of the UK's best-known endurance events, the Three Peaks Challenge.
Participants in the challenge, which the princess completed in June, climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.
Messages from her and William's three children — George, Charlotte and Louis — are played to Catherine by her brother in an emotional scene on England's Scafell Pike.
"They (my children) gave me the reason to get out of hospital. They're going to give me the reason to finish this challenge," she is heard saying.
"Hello, Mummy. I really love you and I hope you do well going up the mountain," her youngest child, eight-year-old Prince Louis, tells her.
"Remember, I'm always in your heart with you... And remember, I love you really lots and lots, and I give you lots and lots of love. Bye," he says.
Catherine, also known as Kate, announced in March 2024 that she had been diagnosed with an unspecified cancer and was undergoing chemotherapy.
Her diagnosis coincided with her father-in-law, King Charles III, 78, also being diagnosed with cancer.
"Navigating cancer or any long-term illness is a lonely road. But it's clear we're not meant to carry life's challenges alone," she says in the documentary.
A message from Prince George, 13, who calls Catherine "mumma", is also played to her by her brother James, who accompanied her on the Scafell Pike leg of the challenge.
HEAL
"We all love you so much and you're going to do a great job," George says, adding that he has been keeping tabs on her progress through a flight-tracking website.
"You look really, really strong. Keep going and we're right behind you," he adds.
In the documentary, "Heal", the Princess of Wales reflects on her cancer experience alongside others going through their own battles with the disease.
A message from Princess Charlotte, 11, is the last to be played to Catherine, who announced she was in remission in January 2025.
"Hello, Mummy. I love you so much. We are so proud of you doing your walk and your challenges. We really wish you good luck and I'll be cheering you on. See you soon," Charlotte is heard saying.
"So sweet," says Catherine, by now in tears, as her brother tells her: "Sorry, William sent them to me and I said I'd play them when we got to the top."
CANCER SUPPORT MEETING
In other parts of the documentary — which will be broadcast by the BBC on Sunday — Catherine describes her time in hospital as "really tough".
"It was a really challenging time, but I feel so grateful because it's really made me appreciate life so much," she says.

The programme also shows her joining patients and survivors at a London pub for a cancer support group meeting, saying it was "lovely to be able to share my personal experience, but also hear your stories".
"I haven't really explored this outside my family walls, really. So thank you for allowing me the time to do that and the open space to explore that."
"Heal" will air internationally via NBCUniversal in the United States on November 30, Channel 9 in Australia on December 1, and CTV and Noovo in Canada on December 7.
All funds generated by its distribution will go to Britain's Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.
